rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Chap. LXXX. If Presbytery shall stand?
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author asks whether Presbytery will continue.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is a political-religious institutional forecast, not an observed outcome.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The circular horary diagram prints 11 March 1646 over 7, at 4:45 PM.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Old Style dual-year notation and historic time conventions retained; no recasting.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Judgment upon the Figure above said
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly offers an interpretation of the particular figure rather than a universal observation of all ecclesiastical systems.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Specific English Commonwealth and contemporary clergy setting.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The figure's angles are mutable or common, not fixed.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not an absolute test; seventh/ninth house method has not been independently recalculated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The ninth cusp is in Taurus, which Lilly treats as a fixed sign.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Fixed ninth contrasts with common angles; do not collapse these premises.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is used as a harsh institutional significator positioned in the ninth house.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Symbolic interpretation, not a measurement of clergy behavior.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly uses Jupiter as a general significator of religion, rites and ceremonies.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source-specific planet assignment.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author says Jupiter is at a station and about to turn direct.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Geocentric planetary state remains unverified by independent ephemeris.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He begins describing Jupiter's departure from exaltation, continuing on the next page.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Physical page seam PDF473–474 must not break condition.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Jupiter is said to have been retrograde for a long time before turning direct.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Prior motion duration not independently calculated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly says Mars currently obstructs or afflicts Jupiter.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Aspect geometry and strength not independently verified.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The source places Jupiter leaving Cancer, its exaltation sign.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical sign/celestial geometry not recalculated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Jupiter then enters the fixed sign Leo.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Future ingress is a separate premise from earlier station.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Upon entering Leo Jupiter passes into Saturn's bounds or terms.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical term system not reconstructed.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: first six degrees obnoxious fixed stars
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly invokes troublesome fixed stars in the first six degrees of Leo.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Star selection and risk interpretation not externally validated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Jupiter next passes into Mercury's terms.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Sequential location; not present-tense Mercury contact.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mercury is called angular and in Pisces, its fall, and the decan of Mars.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Preserve simultaneous contrary accidental/essential dignities.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly names Venus the ninth-house lady because Taurus is on its cusp.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Distinct from Jupiter as general religion significator.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus occupies Aries, described as her detriment, in the eighth house.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Different from her own Taurus ninth cusp.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: twelfth house from her own Taurus
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The eighth-house Venus position is said to be the twelfth relative to her own Taurus sign.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Derived-house relation retained; no calendar inference.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author says Venus must traverse 21 degrees of Aries before Taurus.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Approximate future degree path printed, not measured independently.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: into Taurus she may possibly fix
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly entertains that Venus might become established when reaching Taurus.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Expressly conditional possibility, not firm predictive conclusion.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says Venus first meets a sinister square with Jupiter.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Original square-to-Jupiter premise; inspect glyph in source if recasting.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The subsequent sinister square is to Mars.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Distinct from first square; source graphic glyph may require specialist transcription.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author puts the relevant planets in Saturn's terms.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source claim about term rulership.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says this could have produced significant effects if Saturn were essentially fortified where it stood.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Conditional counterfactual, not unconditional historical result.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if relation Monkery or new religious Order
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He adds alternative conditions involving monastic institutions or the beginning of a religious order.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The author distinguishes this from the Presbytery question.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: not a Planet fixed except Saturn
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly states Saturn is the sole planet in a fixed sign.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Contrasts fixed-placement condition with other dignities.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He calls Jupiter alone essentially dignified among the planets.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Jupiter is simultaneously described as impeded; keep both.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon is described as entering the via combusta.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Historical definition/position not independently calculated.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mars is assigned its fall.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Do not infer physical violence from the symbolic label.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Mercury is also assigned a fall.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Potentially distinct from Jupiter's Mercury terms.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Venus is counted as in detriment.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Cross-check same claim without duplicate empirical signal.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon separates from Venus in the eighth house.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A separating aspect, not a future application.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon next becomes void of course.
rows.original_source_qualifications: An intervening timing phase.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon is later said to square Mars.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Later adverse application distinct from Venus separation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon then squares Jupiter.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separate further sequential aspect.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: not positive or affirmative but conjecturall
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly explicitly calls the judgment conjectural rather than a definite affirmative statement.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This limitation materially reduces any claimed precision or certainty.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: posterity may see verity in Astrology
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He hopes later observers will find some truth in astrology and criticizes clergy objections.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Author's advocacy is not empirical confirmation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn in the ninth is described as harsh, severe, rigid and surly.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Symbolic planet-temperament mapping.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author projects excessive strictness and rigidity onto Presbytery.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Broad institutional characterization without objective rating scale.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He argues such an institution would be poorly suited to English popular temperaments.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Political opinion and horary inference, not a measured preference survey.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly forecasts unusual or frightening internal disputes within Presbytery.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Broadly described events, potentially hard to falsify.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts greed, disputes, envy and mutual malice among clergy.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Multiple vague personal-motive attributions, not independent diagnoses.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Junior clergy members are symbolically represented by Mercury.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Assignment is source-authored, not observed population classification.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He predicts younger members will depart from the discipline's stricter form.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Direction of predicted disagreement recorded.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Elder clergy members are symbolically represented by Saturn.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Not an observed age distribution.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly predicts older clergy will receive less respect for excessive rigidity.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Distinct from juniors' behavior.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects orthodox views to face refusal or dissent.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Overlapping predicted controversy not another independent observation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is described as peregrine and occidental.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Specific historical dignity terms; not independently recast.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: no essential dignity no Fortunes favourable aspects
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Saturn is said to lack essential dignity and support from favorable benefic aspects.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Qualified judgement about institutional strength.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Reception Moon and Saturn but no aspect
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Moon and Saturn are said to have reception without an aspect.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Reception does not imply perfection; preserve negated aspect.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly treats Mercury as ruler of the tenth, representing authority.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Distinct from Mercury-as-junior-clergy interpretation.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says Mercury is separating from Saturn.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separation, not an applying connection.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He forecasts nobles and leading persons moving away from austere ecclesiastical restrictions.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Social group and policy position are source-side inference.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He characterizes the clergy's proposals as a form of bondage rather than freedom.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Author's value judgment, not measured policy effect.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly forecasts that soldiers will dislike the institution.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Marginal author text reinforces this claim.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He also associates Saturn with common countrymen.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Textual astrology personification, not empirical typology.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The Saturn affliction of the Presbytery house supplies Lilly's stated mechanism for opposition.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Symbolic testimony only.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: shall not stand or continue statu quo
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects the structure not to continue unchanged in its then-current condition.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The qualifier 'statu quo' does not mean immediate total disappearance.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He proposes that reducing greed, harshness and malice would improve the chances of survival.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is an alternative or contingency, not a second proven outcome.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: yet it will not stand ita in fatis
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Even with improved prospects he asserts the current form will not endure.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source certainty contrasts earlier 'conjectural' statement; preserve both.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Three whole years from hence shall not passe
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly sets a period of under three years after the question for some change in discipline or government.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Requires specific event endpoint; time origin is printed 11 March 1646/7, not publication date.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Either authority or providence will allegedly introduce a way forward.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Alternative agent, not uniquely predicted cause.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: nearer primitive purity or more beloved
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The new way could resemble primitive religious practice or be more welcomed by England.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Alternative endpoint; not a specific named legislation.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or Authority moderate many things desired
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Alternatively authority may moderate some current ecclesiastical demands.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Crucial disjunction: improvement need not equal institutional abolition.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: for some time not discover what established
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He forecasts a period of uncertainty about the future settlement.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Potentially broad and unspecific interval.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: as when no King in Israel
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly compares anticipated confusion to biblical Israel without a king.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Rhetorical historical analogy, not a measured event.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly expects soldiers or more passionate groups to rise in opposition.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Alternative agent categories permit flexible retrospective matches.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects such groups to withhold financial contributions from the clergy.
rows.original_source_qualifications: A distinguishable fiscal outcome from general opposition.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He additionally anticipates refusal of obedience to Presbytery.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separate collective-action outcome, no prospective record.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects magistrates and the supreme authority to consider or intervene in the matter.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Broad range of governmental intervention.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly forecasts disagreement from clergy themselves and other people of judgment.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Distinct from popular and military resistance.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The author expects England's Commonwealth not to make the current Presbytery its standing rule.
rows.original_source_qualifications: This is not equivalent to no Presbyterian churches existing.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: shall not stand statu quo without refining
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly concludes Presbytery will not continue in its current form without refinement and amendments.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Qualified scope; do not convert to categorical abolition prophecy.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects numerous contentious demands of the clergy to be withdrawn or changed.
rows.original_source_qualifications: No exact checklist of eliminated practices provided.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly offers an alternative reading treating Jupiter as lord of the fourth house.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Same planet plays distinct ninth/general religion and fourth roles.

rows.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon after void course squares Mars Jupiter
rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He returns to the Moon, which after a void-of-course interval squares Mars and Jupiter.
rows.original_source_qualifications: The aspect-order evidence must not be inverted.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He expects the common people to defeat the clergy's expectations.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separate prediction about public reception, not proven consensus.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: He says popular opposition will frustrate the institution's anticipated result.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Source's terminal inference, not independently verified history.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: Following the divider the next chapter opens a question about attaining the Philosopher's Stone.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Navigation marker only, not an LXXX claim.

rows.historical_author_paraphrase: The next square diagram is dated 27 May 1647, 10:45 AM.
rows.original_source_qualifications: Separate horary figure, excluded from this chapter's contents.
